What is automated testing?
Automated testing is the practice of using software tools to run tests on code automatically, verifying that it behaves as expected without manual effort each time.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
Why is automated testing important?
Automated testing catches bugs early, allows fast and repeatable verification, supports safe refactoring, and gives confidence that changes do not break existing behavior.

What is the difference between manual and automated testing?
Manual testing is performed by a person executing test steps by hand, while automated testing uses scripts and tools to run tests automatically and repeatedly.

What is a unit test?
A unit test verifies the behavior of a single, small piece of code such as a function or method in isolation from the rest of the system.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is an integration test?
An integration test verifies that multiple components or modules work correctly together, such as code interacting with a database or an external service.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is an end-to-end (E2E) test?
An end-to-end test verifies a complete user flow through the whole application, simulating real user behavior from start to finish.

What is the testing pyramid?
The testing pyramid is a model suggesting many fast unit tests at the base, fewer integration tests in the middle, and a small number of end-to-end tests at the top.

What is the difference between a unit test and an integration test?
A unit test checks a single component in isolation, while an integration test checks how multiple components interact together.

What is a test case?
A test case is a defined set of inputs, conditions, and expected results used to verify that a specific part of the software behaves correctly.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is a test suite?
A test suite is a collection of related test cases that are grouped together and run as a unit.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is code coverage?
Code coverage is a metric that measures how much of the source code is executed by the tests, often expressed as a percentage.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
Is 100% code coverage always necessary?
No, high coverage helps but does not guarantee correctness; the quality and relevance of tests matter more than reaching a perfect percentage.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is a regression test?
A regression test checks that previously working functionality still works after code changes, helping catch newly introduced bugs.

What is a flaky test?
A flaky test is one that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without any code change, often due to timing, ordering, or environment issues, and it should be fixed.

What is Test-Driven Development (TDD)?
Test-Driven Development is a practice where you write a failing test for a desired behavior before writing the code that makes it pass, then refactor.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What are the three steps of the TDD cycle?
The TDD cycle is Red, Green, Refactor: write a failing test (red), write minimal code to pass it (green), then improve the code while keeping tests passing (refactor).
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What does the 'Red' step mean in TDD?
The Red step means writing a test for behavior that does not exist yet and watching it fail, confirming the test actually checks something.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What does the 'Green' step mean in TDD?
The Green step means writing the simplest code needed to make the failing test pass, without worrying yet about elegance.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What does the 'Refactor' step mean in TDD?
The Refactor step means improving the structure and readability of the code while keeping all tests passing, so behavior stays the same.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
Why write the test before the code in TDD?
Writing the test first clarifies the desired behavior, drives a simple design, ensures the code is testable, and guarantees the test is meaningful.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What are the benefits of TDD?
TDD leads to better-tested code, clearer design, fewer bugs, easier refactoring, and living documentation of expected behavior.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What are some challenges of TDD?
Challenges include a learning curve, slower initial development, the discipline required to write tests first, and difficulty testing some legacy or external-dependent code.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is the difference between TDD and BDD?
TDD focuses on testing units of code from a developer's view, while Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) describes behavior in business-readable language shared with stakeholders.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
Does TDD replace other forms of testing?
No, TDD mainly produces unit tests during development; it complements rather than replaces integration, end-to-end, and exploratory testing.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What does 'write the minimal code to pass' mean in TDD?
It means implementing just enough code to satisfy the current failing test, avoiding adding features or complexity that no test requires yet.

What is the Arrange-Act-Assert pattern?
Arrange-Act-Assert is a structure for writing clear tests: arrange the setup and inputs, act by executing the code under test, then assert the expected outcome.

What is an assertion in testing?
An assertion is a statement in a test that checks whether a condition is true; if it is false, the test fails.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is a test double?
A test double is any object that stands in for a real dependency during testing, such as a mock, stub, fake, or spy.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is a mock?
A mock is a test double that simulates a real object and lets you verify how it was used, such as which methods were called and with what arguments.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is a stub?
A stub is a test double that returns predefined responses to calls made during a test, used to control the behavior of a dependency.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is the difference between a mock and a stub?
A stub provides canned responses to make a test run, while a mock additionally lets you verify that specific interactions occurred.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is a fake in testing?
A fake is a working but simplified implementation of a dependency used in tests, such as an in-memory database instead of a real one.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
Why use test doubles?
Test doubles isolate the code under test from slow, unreliable, or hard-to-control dependencies, making tests faster, more focused, and deterministic.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What makes a good unit test?
A good unit test is fast, isolated, repeatable, focused on one behavior, and clearly named so its purpose and failure are easy to understand.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
Why should tests be independent of each other?
Independent tests can run in any order without affecting one another, which prevents hidden dependencies and makes failures easier to diagnose.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What does it mean for a test to be deterministic?
A deterministic test always produces the same result for the same code and inputs, without being affected by timing, randomness, or external state.

What is a testing framework?
A testing framework is a tool that provides structure and utilities for writing, organizing, and running tests, such as JUnit, pytest, or Jest.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is continuous integration in relation to testing?
Continuous integration automatically builds and runs the test suite whenever code is pushed, catching problems early and keeping the codebase healthy.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is a test runner?
A test runner is a tool that discovers, executes, and reports the results of tests in a project.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
How does automated testing support refactoring?
Automated tests verify that behavior stays the same before and after changes, giving developers confidence to refactor without introducing bugs.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
What is test maintenance?
Test maintenance is the ongoing work of keeping tests accurate and relevant as the code changes, including updating, removing, or adding tests.
You are an expert in automated testing and test-driven development, you are here to help others.
Why is fast test execution important?
Fast tests give quick feedback, encourage developers to run them often, and keep continuous integration pipelines efficient.
